result: In 39 ME/CFS (CDC 1994) vs 30 controls, flow-cytometric NK lysis of target cells was lower in patients (17% vs 31%).
reason: Same measure (NK cytotoxicity), same direction, separate cohort; small and from the Griffith group, so adds little against the null MCAM data.

result: Of 678 TRP/AChR SNPs genotyped in isolated NK cells (39 vs 30), 11 TRP SNPs were associated with ME/CFS, 5 of them in TRPM3.
reason: Another small same-group TRPM3 SNP study (NK cells, not the cited 11 vs 11 B-cell paper); fits the claim's 'tiny, one group' framing.

result: In 25 CFS vs 25 controls, MRI-versus-BP/HR regression slopes differed in brainstem vasomotor centre, midbrain reticular formation and hypothalamus, with no group MRI differences in those regions.
reason: Brainstem MRI signal abnormality expressed as altered autonomic correlations; adds an autonomic angle, Griffith (Barnden) group, exploratory.

result: PBMC microarray found 34 miRNAs up-regulated in CFS/ME, 4 (miR-99b, miR-330, miR-126, miR-30c) confirmed by qRT-PCR and replicated in an independent cohort, most strongly in NK cells; transfecting miR-99b or miR-330-3p into NK cells produced activation with reduced cytotoxicity gene signatures.
reason: Cellular (PBMC/NK) miRNA expression is not covered; omics-ev covers only extracellular-vesicle miRNA. Domain: omics/immune.

result: Pooling 68 female ME/CFS subjects in three duration/age strata, the discriminating cytokines shifted with illness duration (IL-8 high and IL-6 low early, reversed after 2+ years), with an IL-1a/IL-6/IL-8 screen giving 75-88% classification accuracy.
reason: Supports duration-dependence of cytokines but the pattern differs from Hornig's early broad activation (e.g. low IL-6 early), and age is confounded with duration, so extends rather than replicates.

result: mtDNA sequencing of 193 cases vs 196 controls found no pathogenic mutations, low heteroplasmy, and no SNP or haplogroup association with case status, but haplogroups J, U, H and 8 SNPs associated with specific symptoms.
reason: already cited: this is Billing-Ross 2016, the primary study described in the finding detail (only the Hanson 2016 reply is in finding_studies; consider adding Billing-Ross 2016 there).

result: Latent class analysis in 7,041 UK and 1,392 Dutch CFS clinic patients gave up to 6 symptom phenotypes (full polysymptomatic 32.8%, pain-only 20.3%, oligosymptomatic 4.7%); a 3-class solution replicated in the Dutch cohort, and polysymptomatic patients were more severe and more comorbid.
reason: Does not measure housebound prevalence or treatment response; no atlas finding covers symptom-based subtypes (could be a new clinical-phenotype finding).

result: In 76 female CFS vs 19 controls, NR3C1-1F promoter methylation was lower in patients (CpG_1.5 adjusted p=0.0014) and correlated with post-dexamethasone salivary cortisol (rho 0.48-0.54), with no effect of childhood trauma.
reason: Proposes a glucocorticoid-receptor mechanism linked to the dexamethasone/CRF suppression test, extending the enhanced-feedback finding; small control group.

result: Targeted EpiTYPER analysis found NR3C1-1F promoter hypomethylation in 76 female CFS vs 19 controls.
reason: Single candidate-gene promoter, not genome-wide blood methylation or epigenetic clocks; already linked to endocrine-hpa-feedback.

result: In 24 ME patients with orthostatic intolerance tested on good and bad days, LV end-diastolic diameter and stroke volume index were lower on bad days, resting HR was higher, 21% could not stand 10 min, and POT appeared only on bad days in 43%.
reason: Same echo measure (LV size/stroke volume), adds within-patient day-to-day variation linked to preload; Miwa 2016, not the cited Miwa 2026.
